evidence.markupPresent: the prose span DOES carry the canonical role class: c1-01 story idx 4 "habe" has class "rw de r-verb" (data token authored role:"r-verb"), yet computed colour is rgb(31,78,74)
evidence.variablesDefined: --g-verb #DC2626, --g-time #7C3AED, --g-negation #C026D3, --g-genitiv #A06B2C, --g-modalverb #9F1239 all resolve correctly at both :root and the node — the tokens are not missing
evidence.cascadeWinner: two rules set color on that node: ".r-verb {color: var(--g-verb)}" from chapter.css, and ".r-praesens, .r-praeteritum, .r-perfekt, .r-plusquam, .r-futur1, .r-futur2, .r-verb {color:#1F4E4A}" from the page's own inline <style> (line 15). evidence.headColourConfirms: the popup headword takes its colour from an inline style set by renderWordPop (chapter-app.js:2099) using var(--g-<role>), which the page stylesheet never overrides — so the SAME role renders teal in prose and correct in the popup

classA.attribution: production defect (page-level CSS), NOT authored data, NOT the detector
classA.learnerImpact: every affected occurrence loses its grammar colour in prose while the popup shows it — the colour-carries-meaning contract is broken in exactly one direction
classA.confidence: PROVEN for c1-01 (live cascade trace) and for the rule presence in all five chapters (source read); PROVEN by construction that each chapter's swallowed role matches its findings' head colour

classB.mechanism: occurrence role (span) vs lexeme/entry class (popup headword) — two different authorities, both intentional in the engine

codePath.head: renderWordPop resolves normalizedRole from the ENTRY first; occurrence role is used only when the entry supplies nothing ("OCCURRENCE ROLE IS THE COLOUR AUTHORITY … this only fills a genuine void", chapter-app.js:2038-2052)
